summary: Phase 3 (AI improvement loop) + Notifications feature fully tested end-to-end. Backend: 16/16 pytest cases pass (bidirectional ticket notifications, no self-notify, mark-specific/mark-all, rating owner-only & resolved-only, good-example staff-only + idempotent, admin knowledge list/approve/delete with proper RBAC, chat SSE still streams after approved knowledge is injected). Frontend: verified notif-bell + notif-badge, dropdown lists notif-item-*, item click navigates to /tickets/{id} and clears that unread, mark-all zeroes the badge; on a resolved ticket the owner sees rate-up/rate-down and clicking shows 'Obrigado pela avaliação!' state; staff sees good-example-btn which after click shows 'Enviado para revisão do admin'; admin panel tab-knowledge shows pending/approved counters, approve-knowledge-{id} approves the entry (button disappears, badge switches to Approved), delete-knowledge-{id} + confirm-delete-knowledge-{id} removes it. No functional bugs found.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 923 lines — well past the 700-line threshold flagged in iteration_2. Strongly recommend splitting into routers: auth, projects, chat, tickets, notifications, admin, admin_knowledge. Maintenance and merge conflicts will grow with each phase.

NotificationBell polls unread_count every 30s but does not refetch on window focus / route change (only mount + interval). Users may not see fresh notifications until the next 30s tick or a full page reload. Consider adding a 'focus' or 'visibilitychange' listener.

NotificationBell.go(): after marking a single notification read via POST /notifications/read, it does not update the local `items` state (opacity-50 flag), only unread_count. On next open the item still appears un-dimmed until a re-fetch. Minor UX.

PATCH /tickets/{tid}/rate silently overwrites an existing rating (no idempotency check / no 'already rated' response). Fine for MVP but consider returning 409 or a flag if the client expects rate-once semantics — the UI already hides buttons after rating so the API is currently more permissive than the UI.

mark_good_example builds the solution by concatenating ALL staff messages with '\n\n'. If a ticket has many staff messages including small back-and-forth ('ok', 'try this'), the resulting knowledge entry can become noisy. Consider letting staff edit the solution before/after submission, or trim to messages after the last user question.

build_knowledge_context always injects up to 4 approved entries even for chat sessions unrelated to any project (proj_language/framework None). This can bloat the system prompt across all general DevMentor chats. Consider only injecting when there is language/framework context, or when the user message likely matches.
list_notifications caps at 50 items with no pagination — will silently drop older notifications for heavy users.
No DELETE / cleanup endpoint for notifications; the collection will grow unbounded per user. Consider a TTL index (e.g. 30 days) or a delete endpoint.
seed_data_creation: Created several TEST_-prefixed tickets and knowledge entries owned by joao_tk / created_by Carlos during testing. Approved 1 knowledge entry (TEST_p3) and deleted 1. Two other TEST_ approved knowledge entries remain in the DB from prior runs (visible under 'Aprovados'). Not cleaned up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 3 + notifications fully green. Run backend suite: pytest backend/tests/test_phase3_notifications.py -v -o addopts="". Gotcha: the sonner welcome toast at top-right after login briefly overlaps the notif-bell — in UI tests, wait ~4s after login before clicking notif-bell, otherwise the click is intercepted and the dropdown does not open (this is a Playwright artifact, not a product bug). Notification dropdown items are rendered via radix portal at role=menu; the [data-testid^="notif-item-"] selector works once the menu is actually open. Existing approved knowledge entries from earlier UI runs remain in DB — admin panel 'Aprovados' counter will not be zero on next run.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. All new endpoints (notifications, rate, good-example, admin knowledge) behave per spec, RBAC is enforced correctly, and Chat SSE still streams after an approved knowledge entry is injected into the system prompt.
